business_scope.primary_industry_name: Franchise Licensing and Syrups Supply Chain for Bubble Tea Chains

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law with Islamic Sharia as principal source of legislation (Article 2 of the Egyptian Constitution)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt–South Africa Double Tax Avoidance Agreement
Greater Arab Free Trade Area (GAFTA) – Egypt member

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering as amended by Laws Nos. 36 of 2012, 8 of 2015 and 72 of 2016; Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95 of 2016 issuing the Executive Regulations; Law No. 159 of 1981 (Companies Law) as amended requiring maintenance and filing of beneficial-owner registers; Law No. 72 of 2017 (Investment Law) and its Executive Regulations; Financial Regulatory Authority Decree No. 207 of 2019 on UBO registers

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of beneficial owner passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Civil Status Authority / passport issuing authority in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egyptian Embassy/Consulate authentication; Egypt is not a Hague Apostille Convention contracting state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Notary in the individual's country of origin or Egyptian Notary Public if executed in Egypt

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized board resolution or corporate consent of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary / competent corporate body of the foreign shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds evidence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Universal bank or licensed financial institution of the shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Consular Legalization, or certified bank confirmation accepted by GAFI

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, signatories and UBOs against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HMT sanctions, Egyptian terrorist designations under Law No. 8 of 2015 and domestic CBE watchlists. PEP status must be declared; enhanced due diligence is required for direct or indirect PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions and complex structures.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI One-Stop Shop electronic portal (https://www.gafi.gov.eg) for company name clearance and commercial registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Arabic; a Latin/English transliteration may be registered as the secondary name only. The Arabic script is authoritative for legal identification and must be distinct from all existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon GAFI rejection, the applicant or its legal counsel may file a written administrative appeal to the GAFI Legal Affairs Committee within 30 days of notification. The appeal must state the legal and factual grounds and attach corrected supporting documents. If rejected at first instance, appeal to the Investment Grievance Committee under Law No. 72 of 2017 is available before seeking judicial review before the Administrative Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office for a food-beverage franchise LLC. A physical commercial address in Egypt must be established where statutory books, UBO register and corporate records are kept; virtual office may serve only as auxiliary correspondence venue.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-high: approximately 40% probability within the first 12 months for food-industry premises due to Ministry of Health, civil defense and GAFI compliance inspections; unannounced visits are possible for licensed food-service activities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedule and market rate for certified translation of four documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company incorporation and commercial registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; no minimum capital imposed for LLC

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation notice in Egyptian Official Gazette and commercial registry
AML/CFT and UBO profiling service including PEP, OFAC, UN and Egyptian sanctions screening report

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market lease rate for an eligible commercial office address

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended), particularly Articles 1–56 governing Limited Liability Companies; Executive Regulations issued under Prime Ministerial Decree No. 4395/1981; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Chapter 5 (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – One-Stop Shop (OSS); Commercial Registry registration window within GAFI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: LLC Foundation Contract (Aqd Ta'sis Shirkat Khasat Al-Mas'uliyyah) and annexed Articles of Association, filed in Arabic.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital threshold applies to LLCs under Egyptian companies legislation; however, the entire subscribed capital must be fully paid up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited into a temporary escrow bank account opened with a licensed Egyptian bank, and a paid-up capital certificate must be submitted to GAFI. The escrowed funds are released to the company after the Commercial Registry extract is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That upon completion of the incorporation of the Company, all share capital as registered with the Commercial Registry be and hereby deemed subscribed in full by the founding shareholders in the proportions set forth in the Articles of Association. (2) That the registered office of the Company be established at the address specified in the Foundation Contract and that the framing and signboard be compliant with Egyptian law. (3) That the Shareholders' Assembly approves the appointment of [Name], Chairman and Managing Director, and [Name], Chief Financial Officer, as the first managers and managers are authorized jointly to sign. (4) That the Chairman be mandated to open a corporate bank account and to complete any registration or local licensing formalities necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Trademark Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop – Company Names Registration Unit / online investor portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two to three proposed company names in Arabic (and English transliteration, optional) through the GAFI OSS or online portal. The name must include the LLC designation and avoid conflicting with existing trademarks. Obtain the Name Reservation Certificate; this certificate is valid for a limited period and must accompany the incorporation submission.
required_dossiers: Trademark clearance report from Egyptian Patent and Trademark Office (if available)
Signed declaration of no same/similar name in the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity or trademark conflict, file an amended reservation with alternative names; no penalty is imposed. A formal objection can be lodged with the GAFI legal review committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian bank (e.g., National Bank of Egypt or Commercial International Bank) and GAFI escrow verification desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a provisional company establishment letter or name certificate from GAFI and present it to the chosen bank. Open a temporary corporate account and deposit the full subscribed share capital in EGP or transferable foreign currency. Request a Paid-Up Capital Deposit Certificate to be issued to GAFI; the certificate must state the received amount and the beneficiaries (future shareholders).
required_dossiers: GAFI provisional letter / name reservation certificate
Passports and national ID copies of cash contributors
Bank deposit receipt / transfer SWIFT confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the provenance of funds, submit a signed source of funds declaration and supporting bank statements; the deposit may be re-received via official remittance if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Foundation Contract and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Office (Real Estate Publicity and Notarization Department – Ministry of Justice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Arabic version of the Foundation Contract and the Articles of Association. Each founder must appear in person before the notary to sign the DNA and Articles, with their signatures authenticated. The notary will record the date, parties, signatories, domestic server for the LLC, and registered address. Ensure the company name matches the Name Reservation Certificate.
required_dossiers: Typewritten Arabic Foundation Contract and Articles of Association (original and notarial copies)
Valid national ID/passport of each founder
Statement on compliance with the Companies Law and Investment Law
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies errors, correct the drafts, re-execute signatures, and resubmit to the same notarial office; no new name reservation is normally required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop – Companies Establishment Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation bundle with GAFI OSS. Submit the notarized Foundation Contract, Articles, bank capital certificate, name reservation certificate, lease or legal title of the proposed registered office, and the personal declarations of the managers. GAFI performs internal clearance with the Commercial Registry, Tax Authority, and relevant ministries via the OSS. Pay the government fees and obtain an official incorporation approval number.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Contract and Articles of Association
Lease agreement / ownership title of registered office (approved by GAFI)
Passport copies and police clearances of founders and managers
Declaration of non-insolvency and no criminal record for managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query, respond through the OSS case file within 30 days. Missing or deficient documents can be re-submitted without reopening the file. A new submission is permitted if the incorporation application is formally rejected for an uncured deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Registration and Issuance of Extraction
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Commercial Registry – GAFI One-Stop Shop registration desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After GAFI's approval of the incorporation file, the Commercial Registry records the LLC and issues the official Commercial Registry Extract (سجل تجاري). The extract will include the company name, nationality, authorized managers, registered office, and the paid-up capital. Collect the original extract for further tax, social insurance, and banking formalities.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Contract and Articles of Association copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry links the company incorrectly or delays the extract, raise a written escalation with GAFI OSS; the matter is usually resolved by rectifying the registry data and reprinting the extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a concise summary in Arabic containing the company's trade name, type, form, capital, registered office, and the names of the managers and authorized signatories. Submit the summary to the Egyptian Gazette's publication office and pay the publication fee. The publication completes the incorporation process and establishes the company's rights vis-à-vis third parties.
required_dossiers: Copy of the Commercial Registry extract
Summary of the Foundation Contract and Articles of Association (Arabic)
Power of attorney for the submitting agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the returned publication contains a typographical error, request a correction by filing a rectification application with the Gazette office and submitting the original publication certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Card Registration and VAT Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – central taxcard issuance desk / GAFI one-stop-shop liaison
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Commercial Registry extract and company establishment documents to the ETA to obtain the company's tax card (بطاقة ضريبية) and the VAT registration certificate if the projected taxable turnover exceeds the relevant threshold. Complete the electronic tax registration form; obtain EIN (taxpayer identification number) and VAT number. The tax card is required for bank account operation and contract execution.
required_dossiers: Foundation Contract and Articles of Association (certified copies)
Application form for tax card / VAT certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA rejects or delays the application, appeal to the ETA Legal Directorate or request GAFI OSS to perform a follow-up. Rectify any discrepancies in the address or activities in the ETA system.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) – district labor office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the NOSI labor office using the Commercial Registry extract and the incorporation package. List all current and initial employees in the social insurance register and obtain a social insurance number for the company. This registration is a precondition for recruiting staff and signing employment contracts in Egypt.
required_dossiers: Payroll register and list of employees (initial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI disputes the number of insured staff or the registration of the workplace, provide a corrected payroll and premise lease; appeal to the higher NOSI executive committee for review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial License for Beverage Syrup and Concentrate Production (Food-Grade), and Commercial Franchise Activity License

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Limited Environmental Assessment Form (EAF) required; full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) may be mandated if daily production of beverage concentrate exceeds 10 tonnes, if groundwater discharge is proposed, or if the facility is located within a sensitive zone designated by Egyptian law.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4/1994 on the Protection of the Environment and its amendments; effluent limits for industrial wastewater before discharge into public sewer: BOD ≤ 60 mg/L, COD ≤ 100 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 5 mg/L, pH 6–9; handling of empty drums, cleaning sludges, and expired syrups as hazardous waste according to EEAA disposal regulations; use of best available technologies for VOC and odor control at the cooking/filling lines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance from the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) covering the factory, warehouse, and corporate offices; structural safety inspection and building permit clearance from the local municipality (Al-Ahaliya administrative entity); workplace occupational clearance from the Ministry of Manpower and Migration including proving adequate ventilation, emergency exit routes, fire extinguishers, and operational permits for pressurized equipment used in syrup pasteurization, if any.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — official main portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; electronic invoicing and e-receipt portal: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must apply to the ETA for a statutory Tax Card (TIN) within 30 days of commencing business. Procedure: (1) obtain commercial registry extract and certified notarized articles of association; (2) file the ETA tax registration form with a board/manager resolution appointing a resident tax representative, a power of attorney for a licensed Egyptian tax agent, and the premises lease contract; (3) submit the application at the competent tax office (for large taxpayers, the ETA Large Taxpayer Center); (4) after verification, the ETA issues the unified Tax Card containing both the Income Tax TIN and VAT ID; (5) separately register for VAT if taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000 per annum, or elect voluntary VAT registration from EGP 100,000 per annum, on the ETA portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egyptian law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or OECD hybrid-mismatch election; an Egyptian LLC is categorically taxed at the entity level as a resident. Available statutory elections: (a) under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, a qualifying new project may elect a 50% deduction of invested capital from taxable profits; (b) projects licensed in a Free Zone or the Suez Canal Economic Zone may elect free-zone fiscal treatment (0% income tax and 0% VAT on export-oriented activities); (c) treaty relief may be elected via foreign tax credit or exemption mechanisms in Egypt's double tax treaties.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover; voluntary VAT registration available from EGP 100,000 annual taxable turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt enforces a mandatory real-time B2B e-invoicing system and B2C e-receipt system administered by the ETA. Taxpayers must integrate through ETA-approved API endpoints using the ETA JSON schema, transmit each invoice for real-time fiscal clearance, and obtain a digitally stamped, QR-coded cleared invoice before the transaction is legally recognized; a serial number and generated machine-readable code are returned by the ETA as validation. Invoices failing electronic clearance are treated as unissued and disallow input VAT credit; violations carry statutory fines of EGP 20,000 to EGP 50,000 per occurrence under the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 206 of 2020.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports qualify for 0% VAT where the goods are commercially exported from Egypt via customs and physically leave the country. Offshore services qualify for 0% VAT where supplied to a non-resident for use wholly outside Egypt; for the boba tea franchise model this includes franchise licensing fees, royalties, know-how, trademark licenses, and supply-chain management services rendered to foreign franchisees. Conditions: the exporter must hold a valid VAT certificate, issue ETA-cleared e-invoices marked as exports, prove performance outside Egypt, and receive payment in foreign currency through an Egyptian bank account.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs Statement / البيان الجمركي)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure of goods from Egypt
Commercial tax invoice issued through the ETA e-invoicing system
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice evidencing receipt of foreign currency export proceeds
Copy of the Egyptian LLC Tax Card and VAT registration certificate
Signed export contract and non-residency certificate of the foreign franchisee (for zero-rated offshore services)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Article 66 of Law No. 67 of 2016, fraudulent or abusive export zero-rating claims attract a penalty equal to 100% of the evaded VAT, imprisonment from 6 months to 5 years, and fines; previously refunded input VAT is clawed back with a monthly 2% late-payment penalty computed from the refund date, and the offending exporter is flagged as a highest compliance risk subject to intensive ETA audit review.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a partially convertible currency regime. Current account transactions are generally liberalized for trade and services, subject to documentary compliance and CBE reporting. Capital account transactions require prior CBE approval through the licensed bank in Egypt, with Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registrations and profit repatriation typically permitted after verification of the underlying investment and tax clearance. Dividend remittances are allowed to the extent of the foreign investor's share of distributable profits, but practical hurdles include EGP liquidity constraints, long foreign-currency queues during periods of shortage, and mandatory signing of Form 4 covenants for dividend remittances under the CBE's unified foreign-exchange framework. Cross-border transfers in hard currency are conditioned on the existence of real commercial or financial underlying transactions and submission of supporting documents to the corporate bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE regulations, export proceeds must be repatriated into Egypt within a statutory timeframe (customarily within 6 months from the date of export shipment for many merchandise lines, subject to Central Bank circular modifications). There is currently no mandatory percentage conversion of export receipts into EGP; however, for import settlement and corporate foreign-currency needs, exporters are generally expected to offer export proceeds to the banking system, and the bank may apply a haircut by converting a portion of the repatriated proceeds into EGP or requiring sale to the interbank system as a condition of remittance processing. In practice, for franchisors, any royalty and syrup export proceeds must be wired into an Egyptian foreign-currency account maintained with a licensed Egyptian bank, then disposed of in line with CBE's foreign-exchange budget rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / EGP and USD Accounts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs). Foreign fintech and EMI providers cannot open settlement accounts directly with the CBE or provide local banking services without obtaining a CBE license or entering into a partnership with a licensed local bank. Unlicensed cross-border EMI digital accounts are generally not recognized for statutory corporate purposes such as tax registration, import settlement, or OPEX disbursement in Egypt. A global EMI would need to operate as a software-only front-end to a CBE-licensed bank's custody infrastructure via a banking-as-a-service arrangement, which in practice is difficult for franchise operations due to strict beneficial-ownership checks and CBE KYC circulars.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person presence of each ultimate beneficial owner, authorized signatory, and director is generally required for corporate account opening at Egyptian tier-1 banks. The physical interview must occur at the bank branch or with a bank-accredited representative; remote onboarding is only permitted for select low-risk entities and domestic individuals with a CBE-approved biometric/e-KYC solution. A foreign parent or franchisor with no physical presence in Egypt will normally face a mandatory in-branch board resolution ratification date and a video-verified founding member interview before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign ultimate beneficial owners with no Egyptian economic footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original notarized certificate of incorporation, full corporate registry extract, notarized board resolution appointing Egyptian directors and signatories, signed UBO declaration, audited financial statements of the parent, evidence of physical office lease in Egypt and social insurance/government fee payment records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Franchise royalty and syrup cross-border payments flagged as high-risk trade flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Granted franchise license and registered trademark certificate, executed master franchise agreement with bank-approved terms, proforma invoices and contracts for syrup supplies, CBE-Form 4 undertaking for repatriation of proceeds, import documentation (customs declarations, bill of lading, certificates of origin), and a clear tax clearance certificate together with the tax registration number.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial capital injection from foreign direct investment and EGP cash imbalances
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FDI registration confirmation from the General Authority For Investment (GAFI), source-of-funds evidence from the sending bank, board resolution authorizing the capital injection, bank-stamped USD-to-EGP conversion forms if a contribution is made in foreign currency, and a funds-flow statement explaining the purpose as working capital / equipment purchase.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected inbound wire volume inconsistent with declared restaurant revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly projected royalty statements, royalty schedule based on gross sales reports, certified copies of point-of-sale merchant settlement reports, and a transfer pricing documentation file prepared in accordance with Egyptian TP rules demonstrating at-arm's-length royalty rates.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing requires a SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the foreign parent bank directed to the beneficiary's Egyptian bank account, with the purpose of payment clearly stated as 'Capital Increase / FDI Contribution'. The beneficiary bank will require presentation of the GAFI investment file, completion of the CBE's investment registration forms, and submission of the underlying board resolution and declaration of intent. All licensed banks use CBE's unified electronic reporting portal to register cross-border capital movements, and the USD funds are typically converted into EGP at the interbank market rate or credited to a foreign-currency sub-account per the CBE policy prevailing at the time of transfer. The bank will verify the ISIC/industry classification and validate that the receiving LLC's commercial registry permits the franchise and syrups trading business.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Valid outbound clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for high-value supplier and royalty payments and commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for inventory and capital equipment purchases. For key supplier payments and syrup import remittances, the Egyptian bank will require the underlying import customs declaration (or will place funds in a CBE-supervised system pre-approving the transfer against a bankable LC), demonstrating the goods have entered or will enter Egypt in accordance with the bank permit. Royalties abroad may be remitted under the CBE's services payments rules, with a copy of the franchise agreement, CBE Form 4, tax withholding clearance from the Egyptian Tax Authority, and an service invoice issued by the licensor. The LC route is preferred for large recurring syrup purchases because it allows the issuing bank to verify shipping documents and align with CBE's anti-currency-laundering checks before settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla USD/EGP forward contracts with a licensed Egyptian bank for a tenor not exceeding 12 months, subject to the bank's underlying trade document review
FX swaps between USD and EGP executed with the Central Bank of Egypt's licensed dealing banks for liquidity smoothing and trade settlement purposes, not for speculative positions

Synthetic EGP hedges using offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in the limited cases permitted by the CBE for non-resident underlyings, and strictly aligned with a physical foreign-exchange budget in Egypt
Cross-currency swaps for foreign-currency receivables of the franchise (royalty streams in USD, EGP or regional currencies) offered by tier-1 banks under CBE's derivatives authorisation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, generally by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, tax assessment, and statutory late-payment interest may apply. Repeated non-compliance may trigger tax enforcement and suspension of tax-clearance services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GAFI compliance fee and prescribed corporate information update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones and, where applicable, the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally completed during the annual post-financial-year corporate compliance cycle and within the period notified by GAFI or the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Government fees are generally assessed in Egyptian pounds and may depend on paid-in capital and filing type. Non-payment or non-filing may cause administrative penalties, blocked corporate services, suspension of registry services, and eventual administrative cancellation or strike-off after statutory notices; no single universal strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, where submission is required, and the Egyptian Tax Authority with the tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prepared after financial year-end, approved by the competent corporate body, and submitted within the applicable GAFI and tax filing periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare, approve, or submit required accounts may result in administrative penalties, tax adjustments, rejection of corporate service requests, and potential liability for managers and the auditor.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Egyptian LLC is generally required to appoint a licensed Egyptian auditor and issue audited financial statements under the Companies Law framework. Any statutory exemptions or simplified treatment depend on the company's legal regime, size, capital, activity, and current implementing regulations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards apply. IFRS may apply to specified entities or be used where permitted by Egyptian regulatory requirements; tax computation remains governed by Egyptian tax law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain beneficial ownership information and confirm it at least annually as an internal compliance control, and update it promptly after any change in ownership, control, managers, or shareholding transfers. Record each transfer in the Register of Members and complete any required GAFI, Commercial Registry, tax, AML, or licensing notifications.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of members' resolutions and manager resolutions
Beneficial Ownership Register or equivalent beneficial ownership records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 500-2,000 per year, excluding government charges, translations, notarization, and special licensing work
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-8,000 per year for a small operating LLC; higher fees apply to franchising, royalty, related-party, inventory, POS, or multi-branch operations

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic statutory tax holiday for standard urban LLCs. Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 provides optional tax incentives only if the project is registered: 30% deduction of taxable capital for priority-sector investments, up to 50% for labor-intensive projects, and full profit exemption for free-zone entities upon compliance with Economic Substance requirements. A boba tea syrup production or franchise licensing operation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) may qualify for an investment license and applicable exemptions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 37) filed electronically via the Egyptian Tax Authority e-portal (www.eta.gov.eg).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the close of the fiscal year. For a calendar year-end, the deadline is April 30 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: commercial registration number, unified tax number, fiscal year start and end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the LLC's Egyptian tax number only; non-resident shareholders' identities are captured in the shareholding disclosure annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and revenues: include franchise royalties, syrup sales, local point-of-sale beverage income, and any passive income attributable to the Egyptian entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the LLC receives income from abroad, declare the full gross amount; non-resident beneficial owners of such income must complete beneficial ownership declarations to access treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: directly attributable syrup, packaging, raw-material and import costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs paid to non-resident suppliers must be supported by invoices and customs documents; related-party import transactions must be disclosed on the TP form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: payroll, rent, depreciation, franchise royalties paid to foreign licensor, marketing, utilities and legal service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties paid to a non-resident must be separately reported and withholding tax (statutory 20%) declared; treaty-reduced rates require prior approval and a valid Tax Residency Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit before loss carryforward: computed on Egyptian Income Tax Law valuation rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that no expenses attributable to tax-exempt income have been deducted; non-resident shareholders cannot claim business deductions at entity level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss carryforward: apply the 5-year strictly sequential tax loss carryforward against previous years' taxable profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward belongs to the Egyptian LLC only; losses of foreign shareholders or related parties cannot be utilised against the LLC's profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at the statutory rate: taxable income multiplied by 22.5%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No foreign tax credit arises on this line unless an attributable foreign-source profit was included and foreign tax credit is being claimed under the DTA network.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding-tax credits and prepayments: taxes previously paid via withholding on dividends, interest, royalties, contractor payments, and interim instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach documentary evidence of credits; non-resident shareholders are entitled to Egyptian-source tax credits only where provided by treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party disclosure and transfer pricing annex: report connected-party transaction values, TP methodology, and attach TP-1 / Local File / Master File when thresholds are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident franchise-owner transactions must be benchmarked at arm's length; failure to attach TP annex may automatically trigger Audit Directorate review.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form No. 37 triggers an administrative fine up to EGP 20,000; late payment of the assessed tax attracts a monthly surcharge of 3% of the unpaid tax, effectively capped at 30%. Submission of false or misleading information exposes the company to penalties under Articles 108-110 of Law No. 91 of 2005 and criminal-law liability for tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a lower treaty rate, the ultimate beneficial owner of the Egyptian LLC must (1) obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its own jurisdiction, (2) submit a written beneficial-ownership declaration and the TRC to the Egyptian Tax Authority before the dividend distribution date, and (3) complete the 'Relief at Source' application in the ETA e-portal. The Egyptian Tax Authority then issues a binding determination of the reduced rate under the relevant DTA, typically 5% for a substantial shareholding (at least 25%). No refund pathway is available unless the 10% statutory WHT was withheld and the treaty application is timely filed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding: 20% on royalties for IP licensing and 20% on interest on shareholder loans, unless the recipient has an Egyptian permanent establishment. Treaty rates are generally 5% for royalties and 10-15% for interest depending on the applicable DTA; both require the recipient to pass the beneficial-ownership and economic-substance test.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10 million annual aggregate related-party transactions (Local File) for the Egyptian LLC; a Master File and Country-by-Country Report threshold is triggered when the MNE group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 5 billion. The TP-1 form must be filed annually regardless of threshold if any related-party transaction exists.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a standalone 'Economic Substance Regulations' code in the UAE style, but the Unified Tax Law (Law No. 98 of 2023) and Article 119 of the Income Tax Law require a real economic presence in Egypt: physical premises, personnel with nexus, and genuine decision-making locally. Treaty benefits and Investment Law incentives are denied to shell structures lacking substantive business activity. The Egyptian Tax Authority applies a beneficial-ownership and business-substance test to cross-border royalty, interest, and dividend arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of boba tea revenue, fabricating syrup import invoices, maintaining two sets of books, or destroying financial records to avoid CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Articles 136-139, Law No. 91 of 2005: imprisonment of not less than 3 years and a fine equal to the amount of evaded tax, subject to an upper limit of EGP 5 million; confiscation of fixed assets involved in the evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers, and shareholders knowingly participating become joint civil debtors for the full evaded tax plus monthly surcharge; personal passports are seized, travel bans are issued, and imprisonment of up to 5 years can be imposed personally.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham without Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering the LLC solely to invoice franchise royalties from Egypt without any premises, employees, franchise support staff, or actual operational management.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief and Investment Law exemptions; the Tax Authority re-characterises transactions and imposes the full statutory WHT or CIT plus late-payment surcharges; penalties under the Unified Tax Law for abusive transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are subject to personal civil liability for the recalculation of tax and penalties; travel bans and asset seizure may be ordered where the shell was used to facilitate tax evasion or money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring fraudulent royalty or service payments to non-resident related parties to move profits offshore, while the corresponding services are not actually rendered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under Egypt Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002: imprisonment of up to 7 years, fines up to EGP 1 million, and confiscation of laundered assets; the underlying tax adjustment also becomes due with the 3% monthly surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable and may be imprisoned personally; courts routinely issue travel bans and freeze personal bank accounts pending restitution. Corporate veil-piercing is applied when the directors used the LLC as an instrumentality for the sham repatriation scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to engage in arm's-length benchmarking for franchise royalty rates, intercompany syrup supply prices, or interest on shareholder loans; failure to file TP-1 or Local File documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Tax Authority may make a discretionary upward adjustment of taxable profit, impose a 30% surcharge on the transfer pricing adjustment, and impose a fixed documentation penalty under TP Ministerial Rules for non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed deficient TP returns are personally obligated for the adjustment amount if the LLC is insolvent; criminal prosecution is available for intentionally false documentary evidence.
